classificationNotes: Source-draft Deep Ones are treated as a pressure-adapted aquatic visual and encounter-production family. Claims about ancestry, worship, society, raiding, cognition, age, agency, personhood, and hostility are proposals pending taxonomy review. Ocean wetness, coral, native lures, and bioluminescence preserve source identity without making every form Water-affined.
visualConstants: Hunched long-armed humanoid silhouette, wide flat head, lidless eyes, gill-neck, fins, webbed claws, and needle teeth remain legible.
Drowned green, deep-sea blue-black, sickly gray, pearlescent white, and bounded cold native light form the source palette.
Wet scale, eel skin, coral, barnacle, driftwood, rusted metal, whale bone, net, pearl, and shell remain distinct materials.
Pressure bulk, loss of familiar humanoid proportion, and native light-bearing anatomy escalate at explicit source tiers.
escalationAxis: Pressure adaptation and deep-sea command progress from a gasping raider to a sovereign whose court and kraken limbs divide the arena.

constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity ocean provenance, wetness, coral, T3+ lures, and bioluminescence remain aquatic biology, carried material, or habitat—not Water affinity or generic affinity glow.
Wet scales, gills, fins, barnacles, net, shell, rust, whale bone, and bounded native organ light retain physical origins with no elemental substitution.
normal.counterplaySignal: The established gill recovery, coral strap, lure line, translucent organ rhythm, or sovereign court anchor remains readable.
forbidden: Treating ocean wetness, coral, lures, or bioluminescence as affinity evidence

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown; T3 alone first gains its lure; T4 first gains tentacles and translucent organs; T5 alone gains kraken limbs and crown.
Oil-cloth gill collars, heat-black coral plates, ceramic fuel barbs, steam exhaust, and cooling salt seams add combustion hardware without replacing wet anatomy.
fire.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown, so the fuel collar exposes a gill seam; T3 lure marks a cooling barb; T4 tentacles and translucent organs reveal exhaust timing; T5 kraken limbs and crown expose the commanded vent.

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown; T3 alone first gains its lure; T4 first gains tentacles and translucent organs; T5 alone gains kraken limbs and crown.
Compressed shell laminates, sediment scale ridges, crystal joint keys, planted grit, and pale coral-strap faults create load paths without treating native coral as Earth affinity.
earth.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown, so a shell key fractures at the gill-neck; T3 lure marks a loaded joint; T4 tentacles and translucent organs reveal the braced fault; T5 kraken limbs and crown expose the commanded anchor.
forbidden: Mass that hides fins and gills

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown; T3 alone first gains its lure; T4 first gains tentacles and translucent organs; T5 alone gains kraken limbs and crown.
Directional fin vanes, net streamers, gill pressure flutes, debris vectors, and a still throat between pulses create readable force distinct from ordinary sea movement.
wind.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown, so the still gill-neck opens between gusts; T3 lure marks the pressure lane; T4 tentacles and translucent organs reveal the still organ; T5 kraken limbs and crown expose the commanded calm anchor.
forbidden: Floating anatomy that loses ground contact

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown; T3 alone first gains its lure; T4 first gains tentacles and translucent organs; T5 alone gains kraken limbs and crown.
Engineered pressure bladders, shell valves, coherent conduit flow, reflective fill lines, mist jets, and visible drainage distinguish Water affinity from native ocean wetness.
water.counterplaySignal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown, so pressure loss exposes a shell valve; T3 lure marks the charged conduit; T4 tentacles and translucent organs reveal the draining organ; T5 kraken limbs and crown expose the commanded main valve.
forbidden: Treating native wetness as Water affinity

forms.battlefieldDuty: Probe close spacing with a single hook rush followed by a visible gill recovery.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that gasping opens the dull-gray gill-neck after every committed cut.
forms.signatureMechanic: Gasping Hook: the Fishman hunches behind a rusted hook or gutting knife, rushes once, then must flare its gills.
forms.telegraph: Lidless eyes fix forward, webbed claws tighten, and neck gills pinch shut.
forms.counterplay: Sidestep the weapon line and strike the flared gill-neck during the forced gasp.
forms.visualDelta: Hunched dull-gray fish humanoid with visible gills, wet scales, and a rusted hook or gutting knife.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Repeat spear pressure while coral chest armor protects one predictable approach.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the armor strap and fin flare reveal the spear's committed side.
forms.signatureMechanic: Barbed Tide Line: the spear hooks a lane while the opposite finned forearm guards behind coral shards.
forms.telegraph: Forearm and calf fins flare, one coral strap pulls tight, and the barbed spear lowers.
forms.counterplay: Cross the unarmored side and cut the taut coral strap after the spear passes.
forms.visualDelta: Finned forearms and calves, coral-shard chest armor, webbed claws, and a barbed spear.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Fishmen rush along the spear lane; cutting the strap exposes both their gill recoveries.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a hunter that separates gaze from attack by casting its first small lure across the arena.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that lure direction and trident alignment are separate reads and the barnacled shoulder cannot turn quickly.
forms.signatureMechanic: False Horizon: the brow lure illuminates one point while the broad eel-skinned Hunter sets a trident thrust toward the shadow opposite it.
forms.telegraph: The small lure brightens, barnacles grind on one shoulder, and the trident rotates away from the light.
forms.counterplay: Ignore the lure endpoint, cross outside the opposite trident line, and punish the rigid barnacled shoulder.
forms.visualDelta: Broad eel-skinned body, first small glowing brow lure, trident, and barnacle-crusted shoulders.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Tidewarriors hold the false-lit lane; breaking their coral strap reveals the Hunter's real thrust route.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating zones by exposing source-supported translucent organs and routing pressure through jaw tentacles into a whale-bone staff.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that organ brightness announces which tentacle is load-bearing and which flank drains safely.
forms.signatureMechanic: Organ Litany: one visible organ fills, the matching jaw tentacle grips a staff notch, and a pressure-scarred plate seals the selected zone.
forms.telegraph: A translucent organ brightens while one beard tentacle coils around a whale-bone notch.
forms.counterplay: Move to the dim-organ flank and sever the gripping tentacle after the zone releases.
forms.visualDelta: Tentacular beard and jaw growths, pressure-scarred plating, translucent skin with glowing organs, and whale-bone staff.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Abyssal Hunters place lures on the selected zone; defeating one makes the corresponding organ drain early.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-quadrant court where kraken limbs and a crown of lures stage learned lower-form assaults.
forms.teachingGoal: Test gill recovery, coral straps, false lures, and organ pressure while each solved court position removes one sovereign limb route.
forms.signatureMechanic: Arena Command — Fourfold Court: one crown lure names a quadrant, one kraken limb raises its net-and-kelp curtain, and a lower Deep One performs its learned rule; resolving it exposes that limb's sucker anchor.
forms.telegraph: One crown lure brightens, the matching whale-scaled kraken limb lifts, and the lesser court assumes a familiar posture below.
forms.counterplay: Answer the announced lower-form lesson and break the exposed sucker anchor; each broken anchor drops a curtain and permanently opens that quadrant.
forms.visualDelta: Whale-scaled sovereign with kraken limbs, angler-lure crown, net-and-kelp robes, and a court of lesser Deep Ones.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Fishman, Tidewarrior, Abyssal Hunter, and Deep Priest each occupy one court quadrant; solving its lesson exposes and disables the linked kraken limb.
